title: Indian Atlas 036 NE · 1884
source: sources/zenodo-19431985/sheets/036 NE Quarter Sheet Indian Atlas (1884).jpg
condition_note: Intact NE quarter with western hill shading and colored boundaries. Native publication confirms January 1884. Own printed graticule and frame measured.
line_slope_bounds_reason: Native graticule crops show nearly vertical meridians and gently tilted parallels within these bounds.
longitude_convention_status: The sheet prints corrections -69″ and -150″, total -219″, to Madras 80°14′51″. Retain the user-selected working shift -216.18″, 2.82″ east of that total; modern datum alignment remains provisional.
longitude_correction_basis: Printed Atlas-to-old-GTS correction -69 arcseconds, then -150 arcseconds. User-selected working second correction remains -147.18 arcseconds, total -216.18 arcseconds.

printed_longitude_note.transcription: All Longitudes require a correction of -1′-9″, to reduce them to the origin of the Great Trigonometrical Survey: viz: the Madras Observatory taken as 80°17′21″, and a further correction of -2′30″ to reduce them to the latest value 80°14′51″ of that Observatory.

crop_edge_guide_note: Native west-frame-seeds.jpg distinguishes faint inner rule near x386 at y2256 from darker adjacent hill shading near x398.
quality_note: All fitted and withheld observations were checked on the native scan. The two eastern crossings retain residuals of 9.24 and 7.12 source pixels (primarily latitude), while independent checks have 1.75 arcseconds RMS. Retain the selected historical projection plus affine model and expose this local mismatch; its cause is not established.
frame_intensity_limit_reason: Native weakest-frame-samples.jpg confirms faint inner rules in white checker intervals: north x4620,y424 (median minimum 194/255) and west x386,y2266 (214/255). The western rule is distinct from adjacent hill shading. Permit intensity below 220 for this scan while retaining measured frame guides and subsequent native corner/whole-crop review.
frame_stroke_width_reason: Native crop review shows map shading touching north/west rules at NW and lettering with hill shading touching west/south rules at SW. Cap inward dark-stroke expansion at two pixels before the four-pixel inset to preserve adjoining map ink.
